reason: Accepting the fixture's self-signed certificate is a creation option of a context (`acceptInsecureCerts`), and a launched browser's default context takes no creation options. Chromium refuses the per-context form in any case

Playwright refuses a page URL among a persistent context's `args`, since it opens its own page. Strider passes `args` to the browser unchanged, so a URL there opens a tab beside the one the launch opens
Launching without the browser's default arguments (`ignoreDefaultArgs`), which Strider's launch doesn't offer

Playwright's internal `__testHookBeforeCreateBrowser` option, which runs before the browser is created. Strider's launch timeout is `Deadline.within` (option-browsertype-launchpersistentcontext-timeout)
The original runs on Chromium only, where JavaScript coverage is Chromium's
A custom selector engine registered with `playwright.selectors.register`, which Strider has no registry for
Playwright's internal `__testHookOnConnectToBrowser` option, which delays the connection to the browser
Playwright's internal channel call `defaultUserAgentForTest`, which asks the browser for its own user agent; Strider has no such call

Strider won't collect coverage from a browser run: build-time instrumentation, read back with evaluate, works on every browser. JavaScript coverage (`page.coverage.startJSCoverage`), which Strider doesn't have
